relevance.rationale: A survey, so nothing here is new — but it is the standard reference for exactly the machinery the folio's 1-loop / adjoint-torsion work runs on, and that work currently cites only dimofte-garoufalidis2013. QOU/OneLoopEdgeLattice.lean states that the multi-cusp 1-loop construction was validated numerically in part by 'the change-of-curve law against SnapPy's cusp shapes' — the change-of-curve law for the adjoint torsion as a function on the character variety is §5.1 of this survey (Lemma 5.12, Prop 5.14). The folio also has registered entries for the 1-loop = adjoint-torsion theorem (garoufalidis-yoon-2024, ohtsuki-takata) but no reference for the torsion theory itself. Corpus-grep: no ref() entry, no 'character varieties' or 'Porti' hit.

keyResults.locator: §5.1 (Lemma 5.12 eq. (40), Prop. 5.13, Prop. 5.14 as used in Ex. 5.15)
keyResults.statement: For a chamber-regular character, a ∩ [gamma] = d(a* log_gamma) identifies H^1(M;Ad rho) with the cotangent space via peripheral logarithms, giving a change-of-curve law under which the torsion volume form is independent of the chosen peripheral curve.
keyResults.useForFolio: The literature statement of the change-of-curve law that the folio's multi-cusp 1-loop derivation validates numerically against SnapPy cusp shapes; the audit and the Lean docstring assert the law without a source.

keyResults.statement: Torsion behaviour under Dehn filling, with an explicit surgery formula, worked on Dehn fillings of the figure-eight knot.
keyResults.useForFolio: The Dehn-filling side of the same torsion apparatus, on 4_1 specifically — relevant background for the folio's Neumann-Zagier / Borromean 1-loop determinant work (QOU/Knot/NeumannZagierParity.lean, computations/one_loop_torsion.py).

keyResults.statement: Higher-dimensional-representation torsions of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold have asymptotics governed by the volume; the adjoint torsion occurs in the volume conjecture.
keyResults.useForFolio: Background linking torsion asymptotics to hyperbolic volume — the two quantities the folio pairs in its mass law and in the Kashaev/volume-conjecture blocks. Context only; no QOU statement depends on it.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; the folio's torsion apparatus has result-level citations but no reference for the theory itself.
OneLoopEdgeLattice.lean names the change-of-curve law as one of its validation criteria and carries only a dimofte-garoufalidis2013 -- Ref:; §5.1 here is the source for that law.
